County: Susquehanna

Comments: At time of inspection. There were seven wells on site, the Frystack 1H, 2H, 3H, 5H, 6H, 7H, 8H and all of the wells were active. The well was set up for automated production. There was water 3.5' below grade in the cellar with no bubbling noticed and there was no gas detected in the remainder of the cellar. The (9x5) annulus vent pipe was connected to a common vent line that was shared by the vent lines from the 1H, 2H, 3H, 5H, 6H and 7H wells going to a production tank. There was no gas detected in the vicinity of the well or the GPUs. All gas checks were conducted with a MSA Altair 5X multi gas detector that was calibrated on 2/2/23. I took a walk around the location and there were no obvious concerns noticed. There were no violations noted. *Although gas was detected at the (13x9) annulus at time of inspection, it appears to have significantly diminished.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 8/12/2022 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in Somerset Twp, Washington county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 8/12/2022
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 965074
Permit API: 125-28223
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Somerset Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/12/2022
Comments: On August 12 2022, the Department conducted an inspection in response to a spill release reported by the Operator to the Department on 8/12/2022 for the Huffys Family Unit 16H OG Well. The Department was accompanied by Derek Zofchak(Range Resources) and Chase Kolence(Range Resources). The findings were as follows:Per Mr. Zofchak, produced water was released due to a corrisive elbow on production equipment(see photo 9). It was estimated that approximately 10 gallons of produced water was released onto the ground next to the 16H GPU. The 16H GPU failed to be in secondary containment. The Operator has entered into a COA on October 7, 2020 with the Department to install this GPU in secondary containment; therefore, this specific finding of today's inspection is ICS. At the time of the inspection, Act 9 sign was installed at access road. ERP plans were present on site in mailbox. Clean up was currently being conducted with a jack hammer to loosen the affected gravel and then being sucked into a HiVac, into a roll-off box(see photo 6). Excess production fluid, on the ground was absorbed by absorbing pads(see photos 5,7,and 9). Conductivity readings were 5.67mS (release site) and 0.08mS(background reading). The Department request that the Operator submit waste manifests once available. The Department will conduct follow up inspection to verify all impacted material has been removed. Based on today's observations violations will be issued under (78a54, 78a57a, 91.34a and SWMA 301).

Comments: At the time of inspection, meet with Chris McNichols ( Big Dog Energy LLC). Label affixed to well with Permit No. 37-019-21928 (Photo 1). Operator in process of changing out well labels to reflect Big Dog Energy, LLC ownership. The annulus valves at the wellhead are open and venting to the atmosphere (Photos 1,2 and 3). Operator is currently in the process of installing production equipment onsite. The operator submitted an Application for Inactive Well Status on April 22, 2022 and was received by the Department on April 27, 2022. Upon review of information and inspection of the well, the Department has determined that the well meets the requirements of OGA 3214(a)(1) and 3214(a)(2). The application is being forwarded on for additional comments. Violations issued: Since Operator obtained ownership of well in August 2021 and Application for Inactive Well Status was not received by the Department until April 27, 2022, the well is considered abandoned. This is a violation of the Oil and Gas Act 3220(A). Operator is required to develop and implement Emergency Response Plan and review and submit updates annually to the Department by March 1. This is a violation of PA Chapter 78a55(i)5iii.

properties.content:

Violation ID: 8287896
Permit API: 125-23924
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 9/02/2026
Comments: On September 2, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in regards to violations issued under inspection report 4261627.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Department did not observe an Act 9 sign. The Department recommends the operator install an Act 9 sign in accordance with 78a55. The Department also did not observe an Emergency Response Plan (ERP). The Department recommends the operator ensure an ERP is onsite in accordance with 78a55.Upon inspection of the well site, the 2 previously observed corroded production tanks were still present onsite. While the Department did not observe any active leaks at the time of this inspection, the Department observed orange staining and saturated dirt/gravel surrounding the corroded tank. Elevated soil conductivity readings were again obtained around the corroded production tank. Conductivity readings of 5.11ms, 6.24mS, 6.68mS, and OR (Over detectable range, >20mS). Prior to leaving the site, the Department spoke with operator representative Robert Inghram and inquired if there was a timeline for removal of the tanks and remediation of the impacted soil. Mr. Inghram stated that the NOV (IR 4261627) was received and an NOV response was being prepared to be submitted to the Department. With the preparation of the NOV response, the operator is finalizing a contractor to conduct the work and work would begin as soon as they can get it scheduled.Based on today's inspection, violations for the observed release, production equipment onsite not in use, no ERP onsite, and no Act 9 Sign onsite remain outstanding.

I recommend that the Operator continue to follow the Departments most recent spill policy for remediation of spills greater than 42 gallons.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 948135
Permit API: 035-21324
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/16/2022
Comments: On March 16, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline and Brooke Millisock conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The DEP observed and sampled five seeps and four stream sites that were found off the west side of the well pad in "Deep Hollow" along an UNT to Rattlesnake Run. STL Resources revealed that the seeps were occurring and being monitored for specific conductivity and chlorides on March 1, 2022 during a meeting with the DEP. The data that STL Resources provided showed levels of elevated conductivity in seeps 1, 1A, and 4. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling site for pH and conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 had a pH of 8.61 and conductivity of 29.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 had pH of 7.97 and a conductivity of 29.8 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 had pH of 7.18 and a conductivity of 22.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 had a pH of 6.84 and a conductivity of 22.2. Seep 1 had a pH of 5.14 and a conductivity of 308 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a pH of 5.04 and a conductivity of 345 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a pH of 6.62 and a conductivity of 43.2 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a pH of 6.3 and a conductivity of 42.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a pH of 6.25 and a conductivity of 191.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had pH of 8.01 and a conductivity of 28.2 uS/cm. Water quality samples 0651-104, 106, 108, and 111 were collected at the four stream sampling sites and submitted for SAC code 942 plus Aluminum, Lithium, and Bromide. Water quality samples 0651-105, 107, 109, and 110 were collected at seeps 1,1A, 4, and 5. Water quality sample 0651-112 was collected in a channel downgradient of Seeps 2 and 3 due to not enough water available to sample in these seeps. An additional seep was observed up the logging road of Seep 3, this seep had pH of 6.67 and conductivity of 22.5. The previously mentioned seep did not appear to be monitored by STL Resources. The southwest infiltration berm excavation area remains uncovered and the stormwater level in the area as begun to recede eliminating the overflowing of the area. The water level in the southwest stormwater vault was about a foot deep and was unable to be screened for conductivity. The water level in the northwest stormwater vault was about 18 inches and could not be screened for conductivity. The seeps that were observed near the northwest stormwater vault on March 3, 2022 were not flowing at the time of inspection. A new area of excavation was observed where the water from these seeps was pooling. This area has been covered with a tarp. There was water pooled on top of the tarp and next to the tarp. The conductivity of this water was 3,400 uS/cm. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources said they will continue to vacuum the pooling water as necessary. The pooled water in this area could be seen overflowing into an adjacent depression that was covered with a tarp. The DEP recommends exploring this area and removing any contaminated water and soil. STL Resources has removed the contaminated soil stockpile that was being staged on the well pad. Well Pad remediation from the spill that occurred on January 8, 2022 has not occurred. No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, and 3324293.

Permit API: 125-22448
Unconventional: No
County: Washington

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/21/2024
Comments: On 03/21/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Hixenbaugh 1-P060 Well Site following violations issued on 02/14/2024 (Inspection Report 3713663, Enforcement ID 425992). Violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, and 91.34(a) were issued to the operator for the Department's discovery of oil/grease on the ground at various locations around the well site. The following was observed during inspection on 03/21/2024:The larger area of oil/grease on the ground next to the compressor was removed and new gravel was added. Gravel moved aside to view soils beneath - the oil/grease was removed, clean soils noted (Photos 1-3). The section of oil/grease along the side of the compressor fence/tarp had been removed, some residuals noted along fence line. New gravel added (Photo 4).A waste barrel was noted on site; it was unclear if there was waste within, however I recomend that any waste be removed from site and a manifest be submitted to the Department as soon as possible. Containment was noted (yellow container) next to compressor; buckets on containment (Photos 1, 2). Per the operator's response, they plan to remove the waste barrel pending contractor availability and weather conditions (dated 03/07/2024).It looked as though oil/grease was cleaned up next to the compressor and the trough. I recommend that any oil/grease on the ground be cleaned up as soon as possible and the levels within the trough are monitored (Photos 5-7).A small section of oil/grease was noted on the ground next to the piping that previously displayed tubing. It looked as though repairs were made and the tubing was removed. I recommend that any remaining oil/grease be removed from the ground (Photos 8, 9).The disturbance next to the earthen berm was addressed. A liner and gravel were added along this path. I recommend precautions are taken so that water does not travel underneath the liner and cause accelerated erosion (Photos 10-12). A wet spot was noted on the gravel, however this spot did not display elevated conductivity readings. A small area below the berm drain appeared wet; this area also did not display elevated conductivity readings (Photos 12, 13).The production tank was replaced and gravel was added within the berm and under the new tank. There was a wet spot noted below the piping on the tank, however no elevated conductivity readings were noted (Photos 14, 15).The oil/grease on the ground around the wellhead was removed. Clean soils were noted below the added gravel. I recommend that the wellhead is monitored to avoid any additional oil/grease from reaching the ground (Photos 16, 17). Additional gravel added around production equipment (Photo 18).A buffalo was noted onsite, however contents unknown. Although not required, I recommend that this is placed on containment to avoid any materials from reaching the ground (Photos 18, 19).The access road was in relatively good condition. Some tire ruts noted. There was a pile of dirt next to the road. I recommend that this is removed to avoid any sediment laden runoff, as there is a culvert outlet leading down slope and is approximately 35 feet downslope of this pile (Photo 22).Minor erosion noted at the beginning of the access road leading off into the vegetation. There is a spring on the bank below this area. I recommend that this area of erosion is addressed to avoid any sediment laden water from reaching the main road (Photos 23-25). The violations issued on 02/14/2024 remain outstanding. No additional violations are being issued at this time.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/05/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8206968
Permit API: 027-21225
Unconventional: No
County: Centre
Municipality: Snow Shoe Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/05/2024
Comments: Routine site inspection at conventional well 027-21225 with Justin Galiolto of DEP and the property owners on November 5, 2024. During the inspection two leaks were identified. A brine leak was observed coming from an open annulus vent on the bottom of the well head (photos 1-3). A hole approximately 2'x2' was observed at the drip. Large rocks were placed in this hole. I screened the area using a Hanna soil probe and got a blinking reading of 4.0 mS/cm. The soil probe max's out at 4.0 mS/cm.The second leak was observed coming from where the brine pipe attaches to the brine tank near of the top of the 50 BBL tank (pictures 4-5). A wet black streak was observed running down the side of the brine tank was well. Please note that the brine tank was full of fluids. A 5X Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were observed. I contacted Heather Empfield of Diversified Production LLC at ~1230 and made her aware of my findings. At ~1300 Ms. Empfield notified me to let me know Diversified personal were enroute to go investigate the brine leaks. Violations have been cited. Due to the unknown quantity of brine released and unknown amount of time the leaks have been occurring, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 for site remediation.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/16/2022 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/16/2022
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 959603
Permit API: 081-21884
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/16/2022
Comments: This inspection was conducted due to a notification from the operator of a release of an estimated 15 gallons of hydraulic oil from a crane while it was traveling from the B pad to the A pad on the night of 6/15/22. I met with company man Walt Arnold on Pad B initially. He informed me that the access road had already been scraped the night before to remove the hydraulic oil from the access roads of Pads A and B. We then traveled to Pad A where he showed me the crane which was sitting on secondary containment. Next we each traveled back to the B Pad and along the way I stopped several times to inspect the access road. No hydraulic oil was observed on the access road. On pad B, I first inspected the area of the pad which had been impacted by the release of an estimated 5 barrels of produced water on 6/9/22. More fluid was present on the pad surface, as well as on the secondary containment, than was present during the inspection the previous day. Mr. Arnold informed me that it had rained heavily overnight. The fluid in this area of the pad had an electrical conductivity (EC) below 800 uS/cm as measured in several spots. The EC in the sump in the stormwater channel was 742 uS/cm. The EC at the channel outlet at the corner of the pad was 865 uS/cm. Two other areas of the pad appeared to have elevated EC readings. Puddles on the pad surface near the upright produced water tanks closest to the freshwater tank had an EC of 1.8 mS/cm. More puddles on the pad surface near the secondary containment where the coiled tubing unit had been rigged up had an EC of 5.6 mS/cm. The fluid on the secondary containment here had an EC of 9.8 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was in the process of sucking up the fluid from this section of secondary containment. Violations noted for the hydraulic oil release and considered immediately corrected.

Unconventional: No

Inspection Date: 7/20/2022
Comments: On 07/20/2022, The Department received a call from Brian Haner, stating a tree had fallen on a the well overnight and had broken the gathering lines. There was crude getting into a unnamed tributary of Irvine run. An estimated 2+ barrels made its way off site. Upon arrival on site Mr. Haner had booms across the unnamed tributary in several locations. There was a small under flow dam built on a spring seep just below the well. There were also several booms placed at the mouth of the unnamed tributary to Irvine run. Oil absorbent pads were being used to collect oil behind the booms. The crude made its way from the well pad down to a spring seep approx 10-15 feet. The crude continued down the spring into an unnamed tributary of Irvine run approx 140 feet. The spill then continued down the unnamed tributary approx. 1/4 mile. There is some evidence of crude in Irvine run at this time but it is slight. Rain is predicted over the coming days. We spoke with Mr. Haner about placing some booms in a better suited areas. Rain is predicted and the unnamed tributary is prone rise very quickly with small amounts of precipitation. The unnamed trib channel is boulder strewn and very rocky. He said he would move the booms around and monitor them going forward. Mr. Haner also had a excavator in route. He was going to get the impacted soil nearest the well dug up and into containers. He was also going to better construct the underflow dam that was built in the spring flow area just below the well pad. The under flow that was built was functioning but with any appreciable amount of rain it may not handle the added flow.

Smith Well site in Carroll Township, Washington County in response to a spill reported by the operator on 01/23/2025.The operator reported that the check valve cracked resulting in a spill.
